title: Short NFLX — Q3 Revenue + EPS Guide Miss; No Re-Rating Catalyst Before October Earnings
entry: Short $66–$71 at the July 17 open. Netflix opened its AH session at $67.97 (-8.58% from the July 16 regular close of $74.35) following Q2 FY2026 earnings released after market close July 16. The AH decline establishes the opening level for July 17 — enter short at the open or any intraday bounce toward $70–$71. Do NOT short below $65 — at that level the AH gap is fully priced and a technical bounce is likely. Do NOT initiate above $73 — above that level the gap has materially filled and the entry advantage from the guidance miss is lost. Size 3% (medium conviction; guidance miss creates a 10-week window with no positive re-rating catalyst, but NFLX subscriber data is proprietary and may surprise positively).
stop_loss: $77 daily close (~13.3% above $68 reference price) — at $77, NFLX has fully recovered the AH decline and the July 16 regular close of $74.35 has been exceeded; implies (1) the market has forgiven the Q3 revenue guide miss ($12.86B vs $13.01B consensus) because a positive intra-quarter subscriber milestone was leaked or hinted, (2) the full-year guide narrowing to $51.0B–$51.4B is being read as conservative rather than realistic, or (3) a macro risk-on event (Iran ceasefire, CPI collapse) has triggered a consumer tech rally that overwhelms the fundamental guidance miss.
targets: $62 — NFLX breaks through the May 2026 support zone as the market prices the structural gap between Q3 guide ($12.86B) and Q3 consensus ($13.01B) as a trend rather than a one-quarter miss; advertising-tier subscriber growth laps a strong Q3 2025 comp that the guide implies will not be matched; no positive catalyst exists between earnings (July 16) and the next subscriber data read (October Q3 earnings); cover 40% of position; +8.8% short gain from $68

$56 — Consumer discretionary pullback accelerates: Brent at $85.95 creates sustained higher gas prices through August and September, reducing household streaming budgets for price-sensitive ad-supported subscribers; NFLX ad-tier churn ticks up ahead of Q3 results; sell-side reduces Q3 revenue estimates for second time post-guidance; NFLX approaches Q4 2025 lows as the guidance miss is confirmed as a trend; cover 40% of remaining position; +17.6% short gain

$50 — Full bear case: October Q3 earnings confirm the guidance miss was structural rather than conservative; revenue $12.7B or below (below the $12.86B guide), signaling that the advertising-tier saturation thesis is correct; NFLX de-rates from its post-2022 multiple recovery toward 25x forward earnings (from ~35x current implied); hold final 20%; +26.5% short gain
risk_reward: 1:2.0 to Target 3 from $68 reference (risk $9; T3 reward $18)
catalyst: Netflix Q2 FY2026 results (reported after market close July 16) delivered a simultaneous top-line miss and below-consensus Q3 guidance on both revenue and EPS. Q2 revenue: $12.56B vs $12.58B consensus (miss). Q2 EPS: $0.80 vs $0.79 consensus (slight beat). Q3 guide: revenue $12.86B vs $13.01B analyst consensus (miss of $150M, or -1.2%); EPS guide $0.82 vs $0.84 consensus. Full-year revenue guide narrowed to $51.0B–$51.4B. The market interpreted this as growth deceleration rather than conservative guidance — stock fell 8.58% AH to $67.97. The key forward catalyst is absent: the next significant NFLX data point is October Q3 earnings. For 10–12 weeks, the stock has no organic positive catalyst to reverse the AH decline. It must either rally on macro tailwinds alone or wait for October.
thesis:
Netflix's Q3 guide miss is structurally different from prior NFLX guidance misses because it arrives in a macro context that actively pressures its most vulnerable subscriber tier. The advertising-supported tier (ad-supported streaming at $6.99–$9.99/month) was the growth driver that propelled NFLX from $450 to $820 (split-adjusted) in 2023–2024, and it remains the consensus growth thesis for 2026. But the ad-tier's subscriber base is, by definition, the most price-sensitive cohort: users who chose the cheaper option. With Brent crude at $85.95 on July 17 — the highest since the Iran escalation peak — and US retail gasoline prices likely to reach $4.00–$4.50/gallon by August, household discretionary budgets are under measurable pressure. The $6.99 ad-tier is a discretionary expense; it cancels before gym memberships and after Netflix's own research shows the first streaming service most households retain.

The $150M Q3 revenue guide miss versus consensus is small in absolute terms but large in signal quality. Netflix management has a historical tendency toward conservative guidance that it subsequently beats — the Q2 FY2025 and Q1 FY2026 results both outperformed by 3–5% after initially cautious guidance. The market historically gave Netflix the benefit of the doubt on conservative guidance. The Q3 FY2026 guide is different: it arrives simultaneously with a Q2 revenue miss (the first in five quarters) and a full-year guide narrowing (not a widening), which removes the 'we under-guided and beat' narrative from the Q3 consensus expectation. Sell-side consensus will reduce Q3 revenue estimates from $13.01B to approximately $12.90B (split-adjusted for the guide), then mark estimates cautiously below the guide at $12.70B–$12.80B, creating a technical negative revision cycle.

The elevated multiple is the valuation vulnerability. NFLX at $68 (post-AH) trades at approximately 32–35x forward earnings. This multiple was justified by 15–18% annual revenue growth; a Q3 guide implying 8–10% YoY growth in the current quarter does not support a 32x forward multiple — it supports 22–26x. The multiple compression path from 32x to 25x, applied to a forward EPS of approximately $3.50 (FY2026 consensus post-guide-cut), yields a target stock price of $87.50 — but wait, at $68 (not $87.50), the stock is already partially de-rated. The multiple compression is from current $68 toward $50–55 range, reflecting further estimate cuts as sell-side reduces both revenue and multiple estimates in the 10-week window before October Q3 earnings. The counter-party is the NFLX bull who argues: (1) Q3 guide is deliberately conservative and will be beaten, as has occurred for 5+ consecutive quarters; (2) international subscriber growth (Latin America, APAC) continues to accelerate and is not impacted by US energy prices; (3) the advertising upfronts (June 2026) secured $5.5B in FY2027 ad commitments, meaning ad-tier revenue is partially pre-sold. These are legitimate bull arguments, which is why this is medium conviction and 3% size.
bull_case: Netflix reports intra-quarter subscriber data ahead of Q3 earnings (a format they used in 2023) showing ad-tier net adds above 5M in July alone. Or the full-year guide narrowing to $51.0B–$51.4B proves to embed conservative Q3 + strong Q4, and the market re-rates on an above-consensus Q4 guide. NFLX recovers from $68 to $75 by end of July on either scenario. Cover the short before the stop is triggered.
bear_case: NFLX ad-tier churn accelerates through July–September as US gasoline prices hit $4.25/gallon (August). Latin American subscriber growth decelerates on a strong dollar (USD up on Hormuz/September hike probability). Sell-side reduces Q3 estimates to $12.70B in two rounds of cuts by August 15. NFLX reaches $62 (T1) by August 15 ahead of the August CPI print. Continued sell-side cuts into October Q3 reporting push NFLX toward $56 (T2).
invalidation: $77 daily close; OR Netflix announces an intra-quarter positive subscriber milestone (net adds above 6M for any reported month between earnings); OR a major Hollywood studio partnership or sports rights acquisition is announced that materially expands the content TAM for FY2027–2028; OR macro consumer spending data surprises significantly to the upside (PCE +0.4%+ MoM in the August release), indicating the energy headwind to discretionary spending is not materializing
